Meeting Header:
Date: 2025-05-12
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Park (Redwood AE), Sofia Martinez (Redwood SE), Lee Wong (Redwood CSM); Peter Gibbons (Initech CTO), Michael Bolton (Initech SRE), Samir N. (Initech Backend), Tom S. (Product)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be imperfect): quick sync post-incident to confirm RCA and next steps, customer asked for formal doc and benchmark window, discussed dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs for reliability.

[00:00] Jordan: ok hi everybody thanks for joining, um let's do quick round of intros then jump into the postmortem. we have Sofia and Lee from our side.
[00:10] Peter: hey yeah Peter here, thanks. we got a lot to cover, appreciate you moving fast on the mitigations.
[00:18] Sofia: quick recap from our side - timeline wise the incident started at ~03:42 UTC last wednesday when latency spiked and some requests returned 503s, root cause is looking like a KV cache eviction path that didn't gracefully fallback to cold model loads under high seq-len churn, combined with a sudden traffic burst from a customer campaign.
[00:40] Michael: right we saw a cascade - cache misses caused longer token generation times, backlog filled GPU queues and then some pods hit readiness failures, autoscaler couldn't spin up fast enough.
[00:58] Jordan: yes and to be clear we traced it to a bug in our continuous batching code where under certain seq-length distributions the KV cache eviction policy removed prefixes that were still in-flight, so cold starts happened and kv-cache warmup wasn't prime.
[01:20] Samir: sorry can you explain kv-cache warmup - we saw a big ramp in latency then 503s, is that the same thing?
[01:27] Sofia: yeah so when the cache is evicted for active prefixes the runtime has to refill kv cache entries which means more memory ops and some kernels run at lower perf; during that refill window latency can jump. in this incident the refill correlated with the traffic spike and a few pods under memory pressure evicted more aggressively.
[01:50] Tom: were there any network blips or infra events?
[01:53] Michael: we checked infra - no major network outage. cloud provider had no scheduled maintenance. logs point to internal backpressure.
[02:05] Jordan: mitigation we rolled out: hotfix to patch eviction policy to prefer in-flight prefixes, increased readiness probe thresholds to avoid marking pods unhealthy on transient latency, and added a temporary routing fallback to a slightly older model variant (lower memory footprint) to reduce cold starts. that was rolled as a canary then wide rollout.
[02:32] Peter: thanks, that helped. saw the improvements. we still want guarantees: what about dedicated capacity? if we reserve gpus will this still occur?
[02:42] Sofia: dedicated capacity reduces noisy neighbor and gives predictable throughput; however the bug was in runtime logic not the infra. dedicated would reduce one axis of variability but we recommend the permanent fix plus improved monitoring.
[03:00] Lee: and we pushed an emergency config: added an automatic fallback route to a backup model region when latency > 1.2s p95 for 2 minutes - that avoided the second wave during the incident.
[03:15] Samir: are there any data residency or compliance impacts from the fallback? some requests went to different region for a bit.
[03:23] Jordan: good question - by default we honored region routing, the fallback was to a model variant within the same data region for this customer but we documented the event; we can ensure future fallbacks are constrained to same region and only to verified model artifacts.
[03:40] Michael: on monitoring - our alerts were noisy and we had alert fatigue; we missed the early signal. what do you recommend?
[03:46] Sofia: short term: add a golden signal for KV cache miss rate and a rolling queue-depth metric. long term: anomaly detection on p95 token latency and correlation dashboards that join cache miss with queue depth.
[04:05] Peter: also want an SLA credit conversation - we need to understand impact window and compensation.
[04:10] Jordan: noted - I'll escalate to account ops and share the incident impact window and suggested credit calculation.
[04:17] Tom: can you share the postmortem doc and runbook updates?
[04:20] Lee: yes we'll produce a written postmortem, include exact timestamps, mitigation steps, and steps to prevent recurrence.
[04:27] Sofia: technical detail note - the eviction bug was triggered by mixed sequence length distribution; our kernel selection heuristics mis-estimated working set size under high variance. fix involved both policy change and additional guard rails on eviction frequency.
[04:46] Samir: is there a patch version we can pin to? we prefer pinning model stack vs auto upgrades.
[04:52] Sofia: yes, the hotfix is rolled as runtime v1.9.3-hotfix; we can provide pinned config for your dedicated/private deployments and a canary plan.
[05:02] Michael: what's the plan for load testing and verification?
[05:06] Jordan: propose we run a benchmark window with your traffic patterns next week - Redwood will provide load harness and step-by-step plan.
[05:12] Peter: timing ok, let's do week of 2025-05-19, prefer off-peak hours.
[05:16] Jordan: noted. also security questions were raised: do we have KMS integration details and SOC2 artefacts?
[05:22] Lee: we will share SOC2 scope doc and KMS/HSM integration notes; for private deployments we provide customer-managed KMS options and audit log hooks.
[05:30] Tom: any temporary config recommendations? we're thinking about increasing cache size and lower eviction aggressiveness but worried about memory pressure.
[05:37] Sofia: yes, we suggest a targeted increase on pods that handle long contexts and enabling prefix pinning for known hot routes; also allow graceful degradation to model variant with lower mem. we'll share yaml examples.
[05:52] Michael: curious about rollbacks - during the incident a few pods failed readiness because of a probe threshold; what's the rollback path?
[05:58] Jordan: runbook will include rollback steps: revert eviction policy, drain affected pods, restore previous autoscaler settings, and run warmup traffic. we'll include run commands and expected timings.
[06:12] Peter: ok i'd like a one-page summary for execs and the full technical postmortem.
[06:16] Lee: we'll do both. expect the one-pager with impact metrics and timeline.
[06:22] Jordan: to recap next steps: Sofia produces full postmortem by 5/16; Lee updates runbook by 5/20; we schedule a benchmark week of 5/19; Jordan shares pricing and SLA notes for dedicated capacity.
[06:36] Samir: thanks, felt productive. any blockers from your side?
[06:39] Sofia: no blockers; just need the sample traffic patterns and any synthetic payload variance you use.
[06:45] Michael: we'll send that by EOD tomorrow.
[06:49] Jordan: great, thanks everyone. we'll follow up in email with links to artifacts and the postmortem draft.
[06:56] (call ends)
